newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty in no mood to tease c.bank, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Zloty in no mood to tease c.bank, seen drifting.

text.p: The Polish zloty made no attempt to rise above the central bank-established resistance at 2.5 percent from the trading band centre and was seen drifting sideways for the rest of the day, dealers said.

They said that after five days of the zloty's uphill battle against the National Bank of Poland's (NBP) currency buying interventions the Polish unit was likely to wait until Monday's primary T-bill tender before trying its luck again.
"The market is quiet and in the absence of foreign investors I do not expect any major moves today," said Mateusz Bieniek, forex dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.

At 0825 GMT the zloty was at 2.48/2.44 percent from the trading band centre against 2.52/2.46 percent at opening. It was at 3.1475/88 against the dollar, flat from 3.1465/90 at the opening and at 1.8349/54 against the mark from 1.8338/56.
On the money market overnight rates dropped to 5.0/15.0 percent from 9.0/12.0 percent at opening while tomorrow/next were at 14.0/20.0 percent from 19.2/20.2 percent on Thursday.

"Rates fell because banks have surplusses on reserve accounts and they want to place cash for the weekend, with the end of the April reserve next week," said Adam Wrobel, money market dealer at Bank Hnaldowy SA.

Dealers expected the central bank to drain the market with a combined reverse repo and NBP-bill sale operation which could slightly lift T/N rates to 15.0/18.0 percent but said O/N rates were unlikely to be affected.
